reason: The cited evidence (E1) discusses oxygen/nitrogen effects on phase stability and precipitate-free zones in Ti-V-Nb-Ta, a different alloy system, and does not address laser scanning speed, cooling rates, segregation, residual stress, or mechanical properties in AlCrFeNiSi. The key premises therefore lack specific prior evidence support.
premises: Faster L-PBF scanning speed increases cooling rate during solidification
Higher cooling rate restricts elemental diffusion, reducing segregation
Higher cooling rate reduces residual thermal gradients and stresses
Higher cooling rate limits defect formation such as hot cracking
These microstructural changes improve mechanical integrity (strength and ductility)
